s13.title: 694 StuyPulse | Behind the Bumpers | 2025 FRC REEFSCAPE Robot

bet.text: Score as many L4 coral as possible in auto, and design the robot around doing that fast and stably.

demand.text: L4 coral ranked first among the scoring tasks: it scores most, especially in auto, and in week 1 the team figured a robot that does L4 could probably do L1 to L3 (its shooter prototype then could not score L1 at that angle). Scoring automation and the deep climb were also must-do. Shallow climb was dropped: without a deep climb they would rather score to the last second and park.

auto.text: Four-coral routines from both halves of the reef, with paths generated on the fly, plus a one-piece plus two-algae routine the binder calls consistent. The robot can nudge partners off the starting line for the mobility ranking point.

cycle.text: One button aligns to the coral station; the funnel feeds the shooter and an infrared sensor sees the coral. One button per reef level raises arm and elevator, aligns to the closest branch or the side the joystick picks, and scores front or back. The arm stays up until the robot has backed clear.

endgame.text: The deep cage goes into a hole in the robot. Hooks pull it to the center and lift the robot in under half a second, and their geometry and hard stops hold it there after the robot is disabled, without a ratchet.

fallback.text: The climb buttons double as unjam buttons: one raises the elevator to free coral, the other reverses the shooter. Software can switch off a broken mechanism or camera without affecting the other subsystems.

gave_up.text: At the championship the team called its net scoring inaccurate, and it could not take algae from the ground to the net.
The donut climb needs a hole in the belly plate and, in early tests, about a quarter of the robot's area; the bicep climb was thought to have more potential for speed.
Arm motors placed high for counterbalance raise the center of gravity.

changed.text: In week 3 the coral shooter gained algae pickup and net scoring.
The shooter belt loosened over time and got a tensioner. Limelights overheated until each got a thermal pad, heat sink and fan.
Offseason, after the championship: the end effector was rebuilt to lift algae higher and release it more gently.

outcome.text: 47-8-0 in official play; ranked 4 of the pooled top 20 (OPR 114.11, Daly).

facts.text: Coral roller reduction, Kraken X60
Algae wheel reduction
Double-sided belt keeps it compact

A beam break sees coral

decisions.because: in prototypes it scored L2 to L4 at one angle and tolerated almost any feed
decisions.instead_of: a roller claw, which scored slower and needed a wrist or extra pivot for L1
decisions.cost: it could not score L1 at that angle, and the final robot has an arm to angle it

decisions.because: it was simpler, climbed higher in theory (6.255 in against 2 in or more; week 4 design 5.621 in), used one motor and was less affected by the center of gravity
decisions.cost: a hole in the belly plate and a large footprint, though the team then counted it as the same space as the bicep climb

decisions.choice: Passive funnel with a belt wall
decisions.because: the belt wall cleared the jam spot
decisions.instead_of: an active funnel with horizontal rollers, which kept some dead spots
decisions.cost: running the wall toward the entry slowed feeding, so they ran it toward the shooter and planned to reverse it on a jam

decisions.choice: Net scoring from the coral shooter
decisions.because: all 18 algae fit in one alliance's net, and the week 3 idea was to add rollers and plates and roll algae over the pipe
decisions.cost: net scoring was inaccurate at the championship; it used a catapult motion of the arm, which the offseason rebuild dropped

decisions.because: it allows two human players, so the driver must have less to think about
they counterbalance the end effector, for fast rotation with minimum backlash
decisions.cost: they raise the center of gravity

decisions.choice: Hooks that lock without a ratchet
decisions.because: the hook curves lock in place without power after the climb, so no ratchet or lock pin is needed
